entities.summary: Guan Xing, courtesy name Anguo, was an official of the state of Shu Han in the Three Kingdoms period of China, serving under the warlord Liu Bei from 203 CE to 234 CE. He played a crucial role in the Battle of Red Cliffs, a pivotal event that showcased the military prowess of the Shu Han forces and marked a significant turning point in the Three Kingdoms period. Guan Xing's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he also contributed to the development of the Shu Han administrative system, which aimed to promote economic growth and cultural exchange. The Shu Han state's influence can be seen in the subsequent Jin Dynasty, which rose to power in 265 CE and lasted until 420 CE. Guan Xing's contributions to the Shu Han state have been recognized as a testament to his exceptional leadership and strategic thinking. As a key figure in the Three Kingdoms period, Guan Xing's story continues to captivate historians and scholars, offering insights into the complexities of Chinese history and the enduring impact of his legacy.
